content:
sara: Heads-up — CS flagged a customer (acme-inc) seeing spikes of 429s and 500s for ~20m after a marketing burst. They say it started ~10:42 PDT. Requesting immediate triage. @jamal @lucy

jamal: on it. any tenant_id/example request ids from their logs?

marina-cs: i pulled a few from the support ticket. sample req id: rr_9f2b3a, tenant: acme-prod-01. responses were mostly 429 with body: "rate_limit_exceeded" then intermittent 502s. sent full logs to the ops channel DM.

lucy: quick look at infra metrics — we saw a sharp drop in rate-limiter success buckets at 10:41:50, concurrent CPU on limiter pod jumped. Could be a hot-shard or config change.

ops-bot: Incident created: LIM-2026-03-15-01 — Potential rate limiter misconfiguration impacting burst handling. Pager duty notified.

sara: timeline note: there was a config rollout earlier this morning (08:30) that adjusted token_bucket.max_burst from 100 -> 10 for per-tenant buckets as a temporary safety change. not sure if it targeted a subset or all tenants. @kevin, did the rollout include dedicated envs?

kevin: that change was supposed to be for low-tier customers only. I verified the helm values file had the filter present, but the chart patch accidentally flipped the selector to use "global: true". i just checked the git diff: commit 7a1d2c8 (release/limiter-config) shows the wrong matchLabel.

jamal: ok that explains acme seeing hard 10-token bursts. But what about 502s?

lucy: when the limiter started rejecting, the downstream gateway retried aggressively and exhausted some connection pools; those 502s correlate with gateway overload and upstream timeouts. logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:41:55Z] limiter: token_drop tenant=acme-prod-01 allowed=0 requested=12
[2026-03-15T10:41:56Z] gateway: upstream timeout id=rr_9f2b3a
```

marina-cs: customer impact summary: 16% of their calls failed during the 20m window. They saw user-facing errors on a couple of product flows. They want a rollback and a postmortem.

sara: mitigation checklist — immediate actions?

jamal: propose: 1) revert the bad selector to restore previous per-tier policy, 2) temporarily increase max_burst to 200 for acme-prod-01 via ad-hoc override label, 3) throttle gateway client-side retries, 4) open canary to confirm.

kevin: i'm pushing a hotfix to the helm values now to revert the matchLabel. plan: `git revert 7a1d2c8 && git commit -m "fix: limiter selector accidental global"` then `helm upgrade --install limiter -f values.yaml`. I'll add a canary annotation.

deploy-bot: Release triggered: limiter v2.14.1-hotfix by kevin. CI passed. Rolling deploy to cluster: us-west-2 (3/3 pods).

lucy: after rollout, token_bucket metrics look back to expected distribution. acme's rejected count dropped to near zero within ~45s of the new pods. gateway connection pool error rate also fell.

marina-cs: i informed acme that we've reverted the config and that we're adding a targeted override while we finish the postmortem. they asked about prevention.

sara: short post-incident plan items — list here so we can assign:
- root cause: bad selector in helm values caused per-tier policy to be applied globally (human error + no pre-deploy validation).
- contributing factor: gateway retry policy + connection pool exhaustion turned 429s into 502s for some requests.
- immediate mitigation: reverted selector (deployed), temporary override for acme, adjusted gateway retry backoff.
- monitoring/alerts to add: new alert when per-tenant reject rate > 1% for >5m, and a config-drift preflight check for selector labels.
- tests: add unit/integration test for helm chart that validates matchLabels for limiter selectors and simulates burst workload in staging.
- follow-ups: incident postmortem doc, update runbook with ad-hoc override steps, consider safe-default max_burst of 50.

jamal: assigning owners: postmortem -> lucy, helm preflight -> kevin, runbook update -> sara, customer follow-up -> marina-cs.

kevin: notes on deploys: we need a gating job that diffs `helmvalues.limiter.selector` between branches and fails CI if a change widens scope (e.g., to global). i'll draft a CI job.

lucy: small additional action — we should make gateway retries observe 429 token response headers (Retry-After) instead of blind exponential. opened MR to respect Retry-After and cap retries at 2.

marina-cs: acme confirmed degradation stopped and appreciated the timely response. asked for a short RCA note they can share with their ops. i'll prepare a customer-friendly summary after the internal postmortem.

ops-bot: Update: LIM-2026-03-15-01 marked resolved at 10:58 PDT. Postmortem assigned.

sara: recording timeline and links:
- bad commit: https://git.example.com/redwood/infra/commit/7a1d2c8
- deploy: https://deployments.example.com/releases/limiter/v2.14.1-hotfix
- logs: https://logs.example.com/q/rr_9f2b3a

jamal: repro steps for QA to validate fixes in staging:
1) deploy selector config that limits low-tier to max_burst=10 for a fake-tenant
2) blast 100 RPS for 2m from test harness `tools/loadgen --tenant fake-tenant`
3) observe reject rate and gateway retry behavior; ensure Retry-After honored and connection pool holds.

kevin: timeline for CI job and helm test: i'll target EOD tomorrow for a draft, PR invited for review.

lucy: thanks everyone. i'll draft the postmortem and include the metrics, traces, and suggested SLIs. will ping for reviews.

marina-cs: i'll loop in acme with the customer-friendly summary after lucy's draft.

sara: final note: small config mistakes can have outsized impact during bursts. let's treat matchLabel changes as high-risk by default. :warning:

kevin: tracked as follow-up items in the LIM backlog.

sara: closing thread here — add any late notes below.
